desc: This Advantage allow the use of PP to acquire affinity to a single psychic discipline and the matrix powers

nome: Free Access to Any Psychic Discipline
desc: This advantage enables the character to use as many psychic disciplines as they wish using their Psychic Points
The character can see and use magic. They also add a special bonus of +10 to their MR, since their supernatural nature better resists mystical effects.

The character can naturally use one specific Psychic Ability. They are not a true psychic and cannot use Psychic Points to acquire new abilities or to harness the power they have. Their Psychic Potential is not based on Willpower and does not require rolling dice, but automatically is Difficult(DIF). The chosen power can be of any level, but it cannot have a base requirement greater than Difficult. It can be used once per minute without the character suffering a penalty, but each additional use without the required rest inflicts 1 point of Fatigue. Spending additional points increases the natural Psychic Potential to Very Difficult (VDF) and Absurd (ABS), respectively
Players may roll one additional die once they have generated Characteristics and use the result in place of one of their previous rolls. The new number cannot be less then the character's lowest roll

nome: Add One Point to a Characteristic
desc: Add a pout the the value of a single Characteristic
Substitute one Characteristic's value for a 9, no matter what its original value was
Add a special bonus of +25 to Physical Resistance(PhR), Venom Resistance(VR) and Disease Resistance(DR). Spending a second Creation Point increases the bonus to +50
Add a special bonus of +25 to Magic Resistance (MR). Spending a second point increases the bonus to +50
This Advantage adds a special bonus of +25 to a character's Psychic Resistance (PsR). Spending a second point increases the bonus to +50
The effects of this Advantage must be decided by the Game Master
Increase the character's Regeneration by two levels
Increase the character's Regeneration by four levels
Increase the character's Regeneration by six levels
The effects of this Advantage must be decided by the Game Master
An ambidextrous character can perform manoeuvres with either hand. In combat, they suffer only -10 to attacks with an additional weapon
The character may ignore any penalty caused by the dark - except for magically induced dark or absolute lack of light, in which case the penalty is reduced by half

The required number to fumble is reduced by 1. In normal circumstances, therefore, the character will only fumble on a roll of 2. If a character with this Advantage attains mastery in any ability, he will fumble only on a 1 when using it.
The limits of this advantage must be decided by the Game Master

The Development Cost for a field of Secondary Abilities is reduced by 1 point. If the character's class offers a Secondary Ability within this field at a reduced cost, the benefits of this Advantage apply in addition to the class benefit
This advantage reduces the Development Cost of a single Secondary ability for each Creation Point spent
This advantage adds 1 point to the character's Perception when making Characteristic Checks. It also adds a special bonus of +30 to Notice and Search

Grants a character an innate special modifier of +10 per level in a single Secondary Ability. Add this modifier to any other innate class-based bonus the character receives. Spending additional point increases the bonus to +20 and +30, respectively

Grants a special +5 per level bonus to all the Secondary Abilities in a field. Add this bonus to any other innate class-based bonus the character receives. Spending an additional point increases this bonus to +10
The character never applies the -30 penalty for not spending DP in a Secondary ability, and they also receive a special bonus of +10 in all their Secondary Abilities
The character ply applies a -20 to their Notice ability while sleeping
Grants a special bonus of +25 to a character's Initiative score. Spending additional Creation Points increases the bonus to +45 and +60 respectively
Penalties cause by pain and Fatigue are reduced by half
The limits of this Advantage must be determined by the Game Master. In any case, the character will never suffer the negative effects of a trap or an attack determined solely by chance
Grants natural armour of 2 against all classes of attacks except energy-based ones. Although it counts as armour, penalties are not applied for using additional armor layers
Grants a character a natural armour of 4 against energy-based attacks. Although it counts as armour, penalties are not applied for using additional armour layers
Adds 40 points to character's Martial Knowledge (MK). Additional Creation Points increase this amount to 80 and 120 points, respectively
A player can add 3 points to their character's fatigue. Spending additional Creation Points adds 6 and 9 points respectively.
The character sees supernatural things - including magic and psychic matrices - as spiritual creatures. He does not apply the blinded penalty in any of these situations
The character cannot be taken by surprise, unless their opponent's Initiative score in 150 points or more higher than theirs.
The character recovers 1 point of Ki every ten minutes, instead of every hour. Spending additional Creation Points decreases the recovery time to five minutes and one minute, respectively
The character has Elan 20 for the entity they choose. Spending additional points increases the level to 40 and 50, respectively

Characters gain an additional 3 Experience points when the Game Master grants points at the end of each game session. Spending additional Creation Points increases the benefit to 6 and 9 points, respectively

This grants a special bonus of +10 per level to a character's Life Points. Spending additional Creation Points increases this bonus to +20 and +30, respectively. If the optional rules for Between Life and Death are used, this Advantage also grants a special bonus of +10 to those resistance checks (or +20 or +30 if additional Creation Points are spent
When a character's Life Points are below a quarter of their total, they receive a +20 All Action Bonus
The character is no longer limited in the number of familiars they may have bound to them
The character gains an innate +5 bonus to Attack, Dodge or Block, chosen when this Advantage is acquired
The character gets an additional natural bonus
The character gains an innate +5 per level bonus to Wear Armor. Spending additional Creation Points increases this to +10 and +15, respectively
The Development Point cost of changing class is halved

The character can withstand negative Life Points to to ten times their Constitution value, instead of five. Also apply a bonus of +40 to their Physical Resistance Check to attempt to stabilise themselves. Once out of the fine line between life and death, their All Action Penalty is only -30, instead of -60. If using the optional rules for negative Life Points, apply a +40 to the PhR checks
Once per game session, when performing and kind of check, the player can repeat one of their dice rolls and choose the best result
The character receives a bonus of +60 to any Composure Check based on mitigating their emotional state
The character adds a special bonus of +30 to Sleight of Hand, and can apply a +3 to any contested Dexterity Check
This grants a +60 to any Resistance Check related to possession or domination
This grants a +60 bonus to Persuasion Checks related to seduction
The player can increase or decrease their character's Size by up to 5 points during character creation

A character with this advantage automatically ignores any spell cast on them with a Zeonic value of 60/90/100 or less, and mystical effects that cause Magic Resistance checks of 80/100/120 or less. The numbers are for 1, 2 and 3 Creation points respectively. This Advantage only avoids direct effects, not those caused by the spells or abilities affecting other objects.
The player and the Game Master must agree on the abilities of the device. Spending additional points increases the capabilities of the object

The character begins the game with 50, 100 or 150 additional Experience Points, depending on the Creation Points spent. This constitutes a conventional rise in level if the necessary point total is reached
This Advantage provides starting money or equipment valued at 2,000 gold crowns (GC). Further points spent increase this amount to 5,000 and 10,000, respectively

The effects of this advantage apply only to roleplaying. The player must determine the cause of their character's fame at the time of creation. This advantage grants 40 or 65 fame points, depending on the CP invested.
This advantage grants a special bonus to several secondary abilities, according to the character's social position and country of origin.
The effects of this advantage are purely at the roleplaying level.

Besides its effects on roleplaying, this advantage gives the character access to the reserved classes of each principality, without needing to make any dice roll. Its value in Creation Points therefore depends on the level of those classes.
Whenever required, an individual with this advantage can use their contacts to obtain information or limited help within their spheres of influence.
The effects of this advantage apply only to roleplaying.
The effects of this advantage apply only at the roleplaying level.
The character does not reduce their Ki Accumulations by performing passive or active Actions. For game purposes, they always enjoy their full Accumulation, regardless of what they do during the Turn.
Someone with this advantage increases by two levels the Learning Grade granted by their MK.
This advantage grants a special +10 bonus to Ki Concealment per level.

When calculating their initial Ki points, instead of using the basic value of their Characteristics as usual, the character uses only their Power attribute and multiplies the amount it gives by six. The additional points for having a Characteristic value above 10 are also multiplied. This advantage can only be chosen if the optional Ki point Unification rules are used.
The character can develop or learn Mastery Techniques freely, without needing to follow the Tree rules. That is, they do not need lower-level Techniques to learn higher-level ones.

If the character performs no other Action during the round, active or passive, other than Accumulating Ki, they can add +1 to the value of all their Ki Accumulations during that round. Investing one additional Creation Point raises this bonus to +2.
This advantage grants a special +10 bonus to Ki Detection per level.
The character can choose up to two Limits instead of one.
The character does not reduce their Ki Accumulation, even if they are unable to use their hands.
When setting the Difficulty Check of a summoning using Seals, the character is considered as if they had two more levels.
The character applies a +50 bonus to his roll to calculate the result of a Collision against another magic beam
The character recovers Zeon at twice his normal rate. Spending additional Creation Points increases this to triple or quadruple the normal rate
The character does not reduce their MA if unable to gesture
The character can cast spells in complete silence without reducing their MA
The character does not double the Magic Level cost of opposed Paths.
The character gains a bonus of +50, +100 or +150 Zeon per level depending on the Creation Points invested
The character uses their Power Characteristic, instead of their Intelligence, for determining the maximum potential of spells they cast
The character does not reduce their MA when casting spells from grimoires, scrolls or books
Psychic Points spent to increase Psychic Projection increase it by +20, instead of +10
The character doubles the bonus they normally receive from concentration
Any Powers maintained in this way are one difficulty higher than what the character could normally sustain
The character does not lose Fatigue due to failures in using Powers. Free PP and level 3 Powers are not affected by this Advantage

The character Psychic Point recovery rate is increased to one points every ten minutes. Spending additional Creation Points increases the rate to one points every five minutes or one minute, respectively
The character can concentrate to harness a power even while executing active actions.
When the character divides up their Psychic potential in order to use more than one power per turn, they gain a cumulative bonus of +5 for each power that is declared
The character double any natural modifier that their psychic discipline uses. Any negative modifiers are also increased

nome: Deduct Two Points from a Characteristic
desc: Reduces one of the basic characteristics by two points. Limitation: This disadvantage can only be acquired once. A characteristic cannot be lowered below 3.
The character's DR is reduced by half.
The character recovers only half of the life points of any amount they should regain, whether through normal regeneration or mystical means.

They will apply a -50 penalty to any Notice or Search roll that uses sight and a -3 to any Perception check that requires it. This penalty also applies to aim. If they get glasses, the penalty would be reduced as the Game Master sees fit.
The character's VR is reduced by half.
The character applies a -50 penalty to any PR or MR made against any kind of domination or possession able to modify their behaviour.
The character's MR is reduced by half.
The character suffers a -80 penalty to any Resistance against that element and a -30 to all actions in extreme climates.
The character suffers a -80 penalty to any Resistance against that element and a -30 to all actions in extreme climates.
The character applies a -80 penalty to all physical actions that require the use of the atrophied limb.
The character's PhR is reduced by half.
Reduces the character's appearance to 2. Limitation: The character must have at least a 7 in appearance. This characteristic must have been generated by a roll, not freely chosen by the player.

The Game Master must interpret the scope of this disadvantage. In a group, the unlucky one will always be the one who falls into the random trap and the first to be attacked when chance decides who takes the first hit.
The character applies a cumulative -10 penalty to all actions for each month that passes. The Game Master will secretly set a date on which they will die.
The penalties to all actions for coming into contact with that substance vary between -40 and -80, depending on the severity or the time spent in contact with that element.
The character applies a -200 penalty to any perception roll while asleep. During the ten rounds after waking, they apply a -40 penalty to all actions.
The character will apply the fear state whenever they meet the object of their phobia.
The number required to fumble increases by two points. In normal abilities they will fumble on a result of 5 and, if they are a master, on 4.
The character cannot speak.
The character cannot use any ability that requires sight. They always apply the blinded penalty.
The character cannot use any ability that requires hearing.
The character has a 4-point experience penalty to those granted by the Game Master at the end of the session. The additional disadvantage point increases this penalty to 8.
The character applies a special -30 penalty to their turn. The additional disadvantage point increases this penalty to -60.

The character applies a -30 penalty to their combat ability with any weapon other than their own. Limitation: This disadvantage can only be acquired by the Fighter, Prowler, Domine or No Category archetypes.
The character applies a cumulative -10 penalty for each day that passes without satisfying their vice.
Doubles any penalty caused by pain, whether produced by criticals or mystical effects.
Doubles the action penalties caused by fatigue and subtracts one point from the character's base Fatigue.
When their life points drop below a third of the total, they suffer a -30 to all actions until they recover.
When facing a real risk, they suffer the Fear state. If they pass a WIL check of Composure they can reduce the penalty to -20.
They suffer a -30 penalty to all manual abilities that require coordination and a -3 to all opposed DEX checks.
Does not apply the natural bonus per level.
To be interpreted by the GM.
Starts with 100 XP less than the others.
Cannot get open rolls.
Interpreted by the GM.
The character is automatically considered a pariah in all social circles.
The effects of this disadvantage only apply to roleplaying.

Regardless of his social status, the character begins with no more than what he carries with him, and is forced to repay a debt valued no less than 10,000 gold crowns. Another possibility is that he's obligated to pay 500 gold crowns every month.
The character must follow a strict code of conduct, in some way related to his country of origin.
The player and the Game Master must determine, together, the nature of the secret and the consequences that arise from it.
The character must be able to speak to accumulate magic and cast their spells.
The character must move freely to accumulate magic and cast their spells.
The mage will lose one Fatigue point when casting a spell with a potential above 100, two if it is above 300 and three if it is 500.
The character's zeonic regeneration is reduced by half.

Magic can only be used if the action is performed or the condition set by the disadvantage is met. If the action is a secondary ability, the mage must pass a check against Difficult (DIF) to cast their spells.

The character has no zeonic regeneration, so they will not naturally recover the Zeon points they spend. They can only gain magic again by draining it from objects that allow it or from living beings with the Gift. This disadvantage cannot be combined with Slow Recovery of Magic.
The mage cannot choose the Free Access spells of their magic paths and will be unable to access freely chosen spells.
The sorcerer is required to use material components to cast spells. Each spell will require a different component determined by the Game Master, according to its origin and the warlock's knowledge.
The character loses twice the Fatigue points indicated by their psychic fatigue. Limitation: This disadvantage cannot be taken in combination with Resistance to Psychic Fatigue.
A psychic with this disadvantage cannot apply bonuses to their psychic potential by concentrating.
The psychic can only use a single psychic power per round. This does not prevent them from continuing to use others that are sustained, as long as they originated them in previous rounds.
If a psychic suffers a psychic failure, they automatically lose the same life points as the amount by which they fell short of the minimum potential required.
